priorMessages.content: Where is the team losing the most strokes?

Putting is where the team is losing the most strokes, and it's not close. Every one of the seven active players is in the red there, averaging about **-3.0 strokes per round** across recent windows of 11-18 rounds each. Approach play is the next largest leak (team average roughly **-2.35 strokes/round**), also negative for all seven. Off the tee, by contrast, five of seven players are gaining strokes, and around-the-green play is close to neutral (team average about -0.15).

By player, strokes gained putting over their most recent tracked rounds:

| Player | SG Putting | Rounds |
|---|---|---|
| Owen Carter | -2.16 | 12 |
| Ethan Park | -2.72 | 13 |
| Mason Rivers | -3.00 | 12 |
| Dylan Brooks | -3.00 | 12 |
| Tyler Hayes | -3.34 | 11 |
| Jackson Hale | -3.91 | 15 |
| Cole Bennett | -3.92 | 18 |

Cole Bennett and Jackson Hale show the largest putting deficits, but the whole roster is underwater on the green — this reads as a team-wide issue rather than one or two players. Given that, a team putting focus (or a shared practice block on speed/lag putting) would likely move the needle more than individual fixes.

turn.content:
**Ethan Park** is the one to watch most closely.

His strokes-gained total over his last 10 recorded rounds (May 29–Jul 10) averages **-7.38/round** — the steepest deficit on the team — and it's not a stable number. Round-to-round he's swung from **-18.77** to **+0.59**, which points to inconsistency rather than a steady baseline you can plan around.

Three specific patterns compound that volatility, all from his last 11-13 rounds:
- **Approach from 175+ yards:** only 28% of greens hit (25 misses came up short, suggesting under-clubbing rather than aim), well off the ~50% reference tour teams post from that range.
- **Short putts (5-15 ft):** 40% made from 5-10 ft and 17% from 10-15 ft, both well below the ~36-62% reference rates — he's not converting the putts that should be routine.
- **Sand saves:** 29% up-and-down across 21 attempts, with no single failure mode yet identified.

Owen Carter is close behind (-6.21 average over his last 10 rounds) and shares some of the same short-game leakage — worst team approach play at -3.83 strokes gained, plus a documented pattern of short-sided misses averaging 17 ft of proximity. If you can only intervene with one player before Pinehurst, Park's combination of the largest deficit and the widest swings makes him the higher-risk case; Carter is the one I'd flag as needing the same attention next.

Both are already confirmed for the Tri-State Invitational, so availability isn't the concern — performance consistency is.

insights.title: Sand save rate: 29%
insights.content: Across 11 rounds you got up-and-down 29% of the time from sand (21 attempts, 71% reached the green). No single failure mode dominates yet — keep logging bunker shots to sharpen the read. Tour sand-save average is ~50%.

insights.title: Opening hole gap: +0.04 strokes vs round avg
insights.content: Across your last 13 rounds, hole 1 plays 0.04 strokes harder than same-par holes 2-18 (hole 1 = +0.31/hole; matched rest of round = +0.27/hole). 50% of those lost strokes are putting (3-putts on the opener) — a few lag putts in warm-up will settle it. Tour avg is ~0.1 strokes (Research doc §9).

insights.title: 10-15 ft putting: 17%
insights.content: Across your last 13 rounds (88 days) you're making 17% of putts from 10-15 ft (41 attempts) (PGA Tour ~36%). This is your highest-leverage putting band: 10-15 ft is makeable distance and you're 19 points below Tour. The fix is a gate drill (two tees a ball-width apart) plus a daily short-putt ladder — pure-strike reps, not green-reading.

insights.title: 5-10 ft putting: 40%
insights.content: Across your last 13 rounds (88 days) you're making 40% of putts from 5-10 ft (70 attempts) (PGA Tour ~62%). This is your highest-leverage putting band: 5-10 ft is makeable distance and you're 22 points below Tour. The fix is a gate drill (two tees a ball-width apart) plus a daily short-putt ladder — pure-strike reps, not green-reading.

insights.title: 175+ yd approach: 28% greens hit · 25 ft when you do
insights.content: Across your last 99 approaches from 175+ yd you found the green 28% of the time (PGA Tour ~50%, approximate). When you do reach it you finish 25 ft from the hole (Tour ~45 ft, over 28 greens) — that's the dial-in once you're on. 89% of the 55 misses with a distance read came up SHORT — the driver is under-clubbing or decelerating, not aim. Club up and commit to a full number (carry the flag's yardage, not the front edge).

insights.title: Short-side misses are compounding
insights.content: You attempted 52 short-game shots from rough or bunker (60% from rough) with average post-shot proximity of 17 ft — well outside make-able comebacker range. The miss-side pattern is recurring AND the recovery technique isn't bailing you out. Practice short-side flop and bunker splash shots to a tucked pin; the goal is consistent leave-distance, not heroics.

insights.title: Bunkers: it's the lag, not the escape (14% up-and-down)
insights.content: You ESCAPE the bunker fine — 71% of your 21 sand shots reached the green — but you finish 17 ft from the hole and then 2-putt (12 of 15 reached greens). The driver is distance control OUT of the sand and the lag putt that follows, not your splash. Drill: bunker shots to a 6-ft circle (carry-to-rollout control), then 10-20 ft lag putts. Tour sand-save average is ~50%.

insights.title: 125-175 yd approach: 53% greens hit · 22 ft when you do
insights.content: Across your last 90 approaches from 125-175 yd you found the green 53% of the time (PGA Tour ~65%, approximate). When you do reach it you finish 22 ft from the hole (Tour ~30 ft, over 48 greens) — that's the dial-in once you're on. 63% of the 24 misses with a distance read came up SHORT — the driver is under-clubbing or decelerating, not aim. Club up and commit to a full number (carry the flag's yardage, not the front edge).

insights.title: 10-15 ft putting: 21%
insights.content: Across your last 12 rounds (78 days) you're making 21% of putts from 10-15 ft (63 attempts) (PGA Tour ~36%). This is your highest-leverage putting band: 10-15 ft is makeable distance and you're 15 points below Tour. The fix is a gate drill (two tees a ball-width apart) plus a daily short-putt ladder — pure-strike reps, not green-reading.

insights.content: Across your last 12 rounds, hole 1 plays 0.19 strokes harder than same-par holes 2-18 (hole 1 = +0.42/hole; matched rest of round = +0.23/hole). 100% of those lost strokes are tee/approach execution — hit balls before you tee off, not just chip-and-putt.
